criteria.text: The response identifies that the Escrow Agreement's choice of New York law and Manhattan courts conflicts with the APA's Delaware law and Delaware Chancery forum, so that Givand's indemnity claims against the escrow could be split between New York and Delaware proceedings.
The response locates this governing law/forum issue in the Escrow Agreement, Section 9 (Governing Law; Jurisdiction).
For the escrow governing law/forum conflict, the response explains why it matters to Givand and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Pellancourt Cathode Feedstock Supply Agreement requires Pellancourt's consent to this asset transfer but is omitted from the Required Consents, so Givand could be required to close without that consent.
The response locates the missing Pellancourt consent issue in the Disclosure Schedule, Schedule 6.2(c) (Required Consents).
For the missing Pellancourt consent, the response explains why it matters to Givand and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Escrow Agreement's 'sole and exclusive source of recovery' provision limits Givand's recovery to the escrow and so removes the APA's cap carve-outs for Fundamental Representations and Excluded Liabilities (including pre-closing environmental liabilities).
hints: sole and exclusive source of recovery

criteria.text: The response locates the exclusive-source-of-recovery issue in the Escrow Agreement, Section 4.6.
